demo_no_ai_label: Fixed tour and search, no AI. Changes nothing.
demo_tour_intro: A short tour of Create purchase order, Inspection, Availability and Sales. The assistant only opens pages; you perform every action yourself.
demo_step_supply_body: Here you record what you ordered from the supplier; under Receipt you register the pallets. Each pallet gets content lines per variant and unit, with lot and origin, and every registration is recorded immediately with the employee.
demo_step_inspection_body: Received pallets start in quarantine. The inspector decides per content line: approve, block or reject. Only approved stock can be sold; every decision is in the audit trail.
demo_step_availability_body: Read-only overview per variant and unit: in transit, in quarantine, approved and still free after reservations. Kg is never derived from quantities.
demo_step_sales_body: Sales orders with order lines. Warehouse stock is reserved and dispatched exactly per pallet and lot; customer-bound DirectTrade supply is allocated separately. Use 'Find order' to open an order quickly.
demo_search_hint: Searches the existing order list (the 200 most recent orders) by order number, customer name or customer reference.
demo_search_error: The order list could not be loaded. Please try again.
demo_autopilot_label: Fixed scripts, no AI. On this demo environment the tour really enters data.
demo_tour_autopilot_intro: Pick a chapter. In Watch the assistant does everything itself and explains what it does and why at every step. In Do it yourself it points and you do it.
demo_tour_mode_label: How do you want to do it?
demo_tour_mode_watch_hint: The assistant clicks and types itself. Clicking the page is off meanwhile; use Pause to look around.
demo_tour_mode_self_hint: The assistant highlights the field or button and continues as soon as you have done it.
demo_tour_writes_note: Really enters data, recognisable by DEMO-TOUR- in the reference.
demo_tour_your_turn: Your turn: do what is highlighted. The assistant continues once it is done.
demo_tour_paused: Paused. Feel free to look around; click Continue to go on.
demo_tour_stopped: Tour stopped. Whatever was already saved stays.
demo_tour_failed_title: This step could not be carried out
demo_tour_blocker_hint: The assistant is busy. Use Pause to look around yourself.

tour_ch_screens_summary: A round past the four menu groups (Purchasing, Stock, Sales, Master data), without filling in anything.
tour_screens_supply_what: We open Create purchase order: here you record what you ordered.
tour_screens_supply_why: Everything starts with what you order from the supplier; without purchasing there is nothing to sell.
tour_screens_purchase_what: We open Purchase orders: every order with its own IO number, status and invoices.
tour_screens_purchase_why: One list shows what was ordered, what has arrived and whether the invoice is in.
tour_screens_inspection_what: We open Inspection: here you approve or reject received lots.
tour_screens_inspection_why: Only approved stock may be sold, so no bad lot reaches a customer.
tour_screens_availability_what: We open Availability: what is sellable now and what is still on its way.
tour_screens_availability_why: Before promising anything to a customer, you check here that it really exists.
tour_screens_sales_what: We open Sales: customer orders, reserving on a pallet and dispatching.
tour_screens_sales_why: Here stock is tied to a customer, so nobody sells the same pallet twice.
tour_missing_vendor: There is no tour supplier (DEMO-TOUR-…) that Tab can pick. Play the Master data chapter.
tour_missing_vendor_unique: Searching for '{search}' finds more than one supplier, so the assistant cannot choose with Tab.
tour_missing_article: The tour article ({article} with brand DEMO-TOUR-…, code, size, class, unit and kg per package) is missing. Play the Master data chapter.
tour_missing_open_order: There is no open demo purchase order (DEMO-TOUR-…) with nothing received yet. Play the Create purchase order chapter.
tour_ch_order_summary: Record an order with Tab through the line, a date with a two-digit year and a lot; then link the invoice and find the lot again.
tour_ch_order_done: Order {tourRef} (internal number {orderNumber}) is in Purchase orders with invoice F-{tourRef}, on lot {partijNumber}. In chapter 2 we receive it.
tour_order_open_what: We open Create purchase order for our own warehouse. Whoever creates it is the signed-in user (top right).
tour_order_open_why: Here you record what you order from a supplier, before anything arrives. Everyone then knows what is on its way.
tour_order_vendor_what: We type '{vendorSearch}' and take the suggestion with Tab.
tour_order_vendor_why: With a hundred suppliers, typing is much faster than a long list. Tab only takes the suggestion when it is clear.
tour_order_reference_what: We type the supplier's order number ({tourRef}): the number on their confirmation, and the main number of this order. The order date stays at today; we type the expected date with a two-digit year: {expectedDate}.
tour_order_reference_why: With the supplier's number you find the order the way you and the supplier know it. If this supplier already has that number, the screen warns you (without blocking). The date field turns it into dd-mm-yyyy itself.
tour_order_article_what: We type the code {productCode} and take the article with Tab. Then quantity {quantity} and price 12.50; brand, country, size, kg and contents come from the article. Meanwhile the date reads {expectedDateFull}.
tour_order_article_why: You only fill in what differs per line: article, quantity, price. Gross can be adjusted per line (the article stays as it is), and the totals and number of pallets sit below in the same columns.
tour_order_save_what: We create the purchase order. The supplier's order number is shown large; the system also gives the order its own internal number (IO-year-sequence).
tour_order_save_why: Everyone finds the order by the supplier's number; the internal number stays in the background, also for an order without a supplier number.
tour_order_find_what: We go to Purchase orders, search for the supplier's order number ({tourRef}) and open the order.
tour_order_find_why: Per order you see what was ordered, what has arrived and whether the invoice is in.
tour_order_invoice_what: The supplier's invoice has arrived. We record invoice number F-{tourRef} with this order.
tour_order_invoice_why: You see which orders are invoiced and never pay twice. The same number cannot be added twice to one order.
tour_order_by-invoice_what: We now search for invoice number F-{tourRef}; the order comes right back.
tour_order_by-invoice_why: If a question about an invoice comes up later, you find the matching order straight away.
tour_ch_receive_summary: Enter blind what arrives, inspect with Who assesses, reject a part with reason and decision, and see what is sellable.
tour_ch_receive_done: Lot {lot} of {orderNumber} is received and approved; {rejectQuantity} go back to the supplier and a credit note is expected.
tour_receive_open_what: We open Receipt and look up the demo purchase order {orderNumber}.
tour_receive_open_why: You always receive a pallet against what was ordered, so stock matches purchasing.
tour_receive_line_what: We tick the line and fill in what it says: origin, size and packaging, {quantity} pieces and the kg per package. Lot {lot} comes from the purchase order (without a lot we type it ourselves).
tour_receive_line_why: The order is deliberately not shown first: who fills in themselves, really looks. If everything matches, the system books without questions.
tour_receive_register_what: We register the pallet. The lot is now in quarantine.
tour_receive_register_why: What comes in is not inspected yet and may not be sold yet.
tour_receive_inspector_what: We go to the inspection of this pallet.
tour_receive_inspector_why: Every quality decision carries a name, so you know later who decided what.
tour_receive_approve_what: We approve lot {lot}. At the inspection itself we choose who assesses: {actor}.
tour_receive_approve_why: Only after approval does the stock count as sellable. The history records both who assessed and who was signed in.
tour_receive_reject_what: On a closer look {rejectQuantity} are not good. We reject that part with reason Quality and decision Return to supplier.
tour_receive_reject_why: Return: the supplier collects it. Claim discount: you keep the lot (blocked, can be released later). Dispose: throw away. After return or discount the order shows 'Credit note expected'.
tour_receive_availability_what: Availability shows what of this article is sellable right now.
tour_receive_availability_why: Only approved stock counts; quarantine, blocked and rejected do not. Nobody promises a customer what may not be sold.
tour_missing_customer: There is no tour customer (DEMO-TOUR-…) that Tab can pick. Play the Master data chapter.
tour_missing_stock: There is no approved warehouse stock of {article} (at least {quantity}) to reserve.
tour_ch_sales_summary: A sales order with SO number and customer reference, reserve stock with the purchase order, lot and pallet per piece, and dispatch.
tour_ch_sales_done: Sales order {salesNumber} ({tourRef}) for {customerName} has been reserved on an approved pallet and dispatched.
tour_sales_new_what: We create a new sales order. Whoever creates it is the signed-in user (top right).
tour_sales_new_why: An order records what the customer wants and when.
tour_sales_customer_what: We type '{customerSearch}' and take the top customer with Tab ({customerName}). Then customer reference {tourRef} and the delivery date.
tour_sales_customer_why: Customers often quote their own order number. You put it in the customer reference so you find the order again later.
tour_sales_line_what: The tour article (code {productCode}), quantity {salesQuantity}. The system fills in the unit and kg from the article.
tour_sales_line_why: You sell in packages, but customer and carrier also count in kg. No calculating needed.
tour_sales_save_what: We save the order: it gets its own number (SO-…). Then we open it to reserve stock.
tour_sales_save_why: From now on everyone sees the order and it can be handled further.
tour_sales_stock_what: We choose stock: the assistant points at an approved pallet that holds the quantity.
tour_sales_stock_why: You always reserve on a real pallet and lot, not on a number out of thin air.
tour_sales_reserve_what: We reserve {salesQuantity} for this customer and confirm.
tour_sales_reserve_why: Reserving means: this stock is for this customer. Nobody else sells it too, and you know which lot and GGN goes there.
tour_sales_dispatch_what: We dispatch the order with all reserved lines.
tour_sales_dispatch_why: On dispatch the stock really leaves the pallet; the reservation becomes a dispatch.
tour_sales_summary_title: What is in the system now?
tour_sales_summary_what: Sales order {salesNumber} for {customerName}: reserved on an approved pallet and dispatched.
tour_sales_summary_why: From purchase to dispatch everything is traceable: which lot, from which supplier, to which customer.

articles_used_by_sales: Sales order: packaging unit and packages per pallet (CPP) for pallet entry.
articles_used_by_supply: Purchase order and receipt: weight method and net kg per package, CPP for pallet entry.

relations_save_hint: Only the company name is required. Changes never touch stored document values.
relations_role_added: Role added to {name}; existing numbers stay the same.
relations_inactive_hint: Inactive: historical documents stay readable, new documents for this relation are refused.

relations_hint_country: ISO country code, 2 letters (NL, DE, BE, …).

relations_contacts_hint: Several phone numbers and e-mail addresses with a label per person. A role does not yet decide which documents someone receives; document recipients follow separately.

relations_ggn_hint: One supplier may represent several producers. As stated; a format check is not a certificate check. A CoC number is not a GGN. On receipt a number is only proposed automatically when exactly one is active.

relations_note_hint: Internal only; never on documents, e-mails or exports.

relations_error_country_required: Choose the country (2 letters), also for foreign addresses.

intro_purchase_orders: All purchase orders with their receipts, inspection and invoices. Create a new order with "Create purchase order".
intro_purchase_order_new: You record what you ordered. Then you receive the goods under Receipt.
intro_receipts: You register the pallets that arrive against a purchase order. Then you inspect them under Inspection.
intro_direct_trade: Customer-bound supply goes straight from the supplier to the customer and never becomes stock. Then you allocate it on the sales order.
tour_ch_chain_summary: The chain strip on purchase order, receipt and sales order, and the lot under Stock › Lots: this is how you click through the whole chain.
tour_ch_chain_done: This is how every document shows where it is in the chain. Click a block to go to that step.
tour_missing_chain: There is no demo purchase order with a lot that has been sold from yet.
tour_chain_strip_what: At the top of purchase order {orderNumber} is the chain: purchase order, receipt, inspection, stock, sale, delivery and invoice.
tour_chain_strip_why: You see at a glance where the order stands, without visiting every screen.
tour_chain_progress_what: Each block shows the status and the quantities, for example how much was approved or rejected.
tour_chain_progress_why: Green is done, orange partly, grey nothing yet or not available yet.
tour_chain_sold_what: Under Sales order and Delivery are the sales orders that reserve or dispatched from this purchase order.
tour_chain_sold_why: Each block is a link: click and you are on that sales order.
tour_chain_origin_what: On the sales order the bar points back: the purchase order and the lot the reserved stock comes from.
tour_chain_origin_why: So the origin stays visible, from sale back to purchase.
sales_next_reserve: Next step: reserve approved stock per line ("Choose stock and reserve"), or allocate customer-bound supply.
sales_next_dispatch: Next step: dispatch the reserved stock ("Dispatch" at the top).
sales_next_confirm: Next step: everything is dispatched; confirm delivery on the dispatch.
sales_next_done: Everything is dispatched and delivered. The invoice comes in a later version.
availability_view_hint_sales: Free to sell = stock + expected − sold. A negative number is a shortage: you may sell, it recovers as soon as purchases arrive.
sales_balance_failed: Stock could not be loaded; the system checks it when you save.
sales_split_line: Split: {stock} from stock, {expected} from expected supply
sales_shortage_warning: You sell {quantity} {unit} more than stock and expected supply. That is allowed; the order shows a shortage.
sales_shortage_saved: You sell {quantity} {unit} more than stock and expected supply ({name}). The order shows a shortage until purchases arrive.
sales_fifo_hint: Proposal by receipt date, then lot number. Change the quantities if you want another lot; you confirm yourself.
sales_fifo_no_stock: No approved stock of this article is free right now. The line keeps waiting for stock.
sales_fifo_total: Together {total} of the {needed} {unit} this line still needs.
sales_awaiting_empty: No lines sold before arrival that can be reserved now.
tour_ch_presell_summary: Read Availability, sell more than there is with Sell (Shortage, no block), receive and inspect, then reserve oldest lot first.
tour_ch_presell_done: Sales order {salesNumber} for {customerName} was sold before arrival, then reserved on the oldest lot. The shortage stays visible until more is purchased.
tour_presell_free_what: In Availability you see per article Stock, Expected, Sold and Free to sell.
tour_presell_free_why: Free = stock + expected − sold. You may also sell what is still on its way; a negative number is a shortage.
tour_presell_sell_what: With Sell a new sales order opens with this article. We pick the customer, type {sellQuantity} (more than free) and choose From expected supply. The same works directly via Sales orders › New sales order.
tour_presell_sell_why: A shortage is a warning, not a block. If there is some stock already, you can split the line over stock and expected supply.
tour_presell_save_what: The order gets its own number (VO-…) and a clear message how much more is sold than is here and coming.
tour_presell_save_why: So purchasing knows right away more is needed, and the order shows a shortage until then.
tour_presell_worklist_what: The goods are in and approved. This worklist shows the lines you can reserve now.
tour_presell_worklist_why: The system never reserves by itself: you confirm which pallets belong to which order.
tour_presell_reserve_what: We open the order and choose Reserve (oldest lot first). The proposal follows the receipt date; you can change it.
tour_presell_reserve_why: Each reservation stays on an exact pallet and lot: you can always see which purchase order it came from.
tour_presell_chain_what: At the top of the order you see the purchase orders it comes from, and what still waits for a purchase order.
tour_presell_chain_why: The shortage goes back to zero as soon as purchases arrive; then you can reserve the rest too.
settings_partij_hint: How a new lot gets its number. A number that already exists (also with other spaces, hyphens or capitals) never becomes a second lot.
settings_partij_mode_auto: Suggest: the system fills in the next number, you may overwrite it
settings_partij_mode_own: Own number: you always type the lot number yourself
settings_partij_format_hint: Placeholders: {placeholders} (year 2 digits, year 4 digits, month, sequence). Fixed text may go before or after, for example 5{JJ}{MM}{volgnr}.
settings_partij_format_error_sequence_on: The format needs {volgnr} exactly once, otherwise two lots get the same number.
settings_partij_example_own: With Own number this is not suggested; the format only applies when you choose Suggest again.
partij_hint_suggested: Suggested number. You may type your own number.
partij_hint_existing: Existing lot ({vendors}). This order is added to it.
partij_hint_own: Own number. If it exists already, the screen asks whether to use that lot.
partij_exists_question: Lot {number} already exists, do you want to use it?
partij_search: Search by lot number, product or supplier
partij_supplier_lot_hint: The lot number the supplier puts on the boxes. Not their order number and not our own lot.
partij_saved_without: Saved without a lot. You can choose one later on the purchase order or at receipt.
partij_none_warning: No lot yet. You can save like this and choose the lot later, on the purchase order or at receipt.
partij_link_none: Purchase order {order} has no lot yet.
partij_link_reason_hint: Goods have already been received: the received pallets get this lot, with your reason in the history. Their lot number stays.
partij_receipt_without_hint: Without a lot you type the lot number yourself, as before.
intro_partijen: Every load with its lot number: the purchase orders, receipts, stock and sales that belong to it.
partij_list_search_placeholder: Lot number, supplier's lot, product or supplier
partij_orders_none: No purchase order on this lot yet.
partij_sales_none: No sales reserving or delivering from this lot yet.
partij_correct_exists: Lot {number} already exists. Choose another number.
partij_fixed_hint: A purchase order or receipt is linked to this lot: the number only changes with a correction and a reason, and the lot can no longer be deleted.
tour_order_partij_what: Below the dates is the suggested lot number for this shipment; you may type your own. With Choose existing lot you put a second order on the same lot. Next to it we type the supplier's lot.
tour_order_partij_why: Everything revolves around the lot number: purchasing, receiving and sales of this shipment hang from it. If a shipment comes from two suppliers, both orders get the same lot.
tour_order_lot_what: Under Stock › Lots we search lot {partijNumber}. Its detail shows this purchase order; receipts and sales follow later.
tour_order_lot_why: A lot can have several purchase orders, for example a load with goods from two suppliers.
first_missing_vendor: There is no supplier yet. Add a supplier first.
first_missing_customer: There is no customer yet. Add a customer first.
first_missing_article: There are no articles yet. Create an article first.
start_begin_intro: The system is still empty. This is how you start:
start_begin_relations: Create relations: your suppliers and customers
start_begin_articles: Create articles: what you buy and sell
relations_empty_text: Your suppliers and customers are listed here; you record each relation once.
articles_empty_text: An article is what you buy and sell, with origin, size and class; on purchases and sales you then pick it by its code.
po_empty_text: This shows what you ordered from your suppliers, until it has arrived and been inspected.
partij_empty_text: A lot starts with the first purchase order; after that you see everything that belongs to that shipment here.
receipts_empty_text: Receiving is always against a purchase order: create one first.
purchase_empty_text: Your suppliers' invoices appear here, with total, due date and status.
receipts_empty_title: No open purchase order to receive yet
demo_tour_skipped: {count} steps skipped: what they create already existed.
tour_screens_receipts_what: We open Receiving: this is where you register incoming pallets, always against a purchase order.
tour_screens_receipts_why: You enter what is actually there; if it differs from the order, the system asks whether that is right.
tour_screens_partijen_what: We open Stock › Lots: every shipment with its lot number, and everything that belongs to it.
tour_screens_partijen_why: Purchasing, receiving, stock and sales of one shipment are kept together.
tour_screens_direct-trade_what: We open Customer-bound supply: goods that go straight from the supplier to one customer.
tour_screens_direct-trade_why: They never become warehouse stock and are therefore never shown as free to sell.
tour_screens_relations_what: We open Master data › Relations: your suppliers and customers, each recorded once.
tour_screens_relations_why: Every purchase order has a supplier and every sales order a customer; you pick them from here.
tour_screens_articles_what: We open Master data › Articles: what you buy and sell, with origin, size, class and packaging.
tour_screens_articles_why: With the code you pick the article on every order; its defaults come along automatically.
tour_ch_master_summary: A supplier and a customer with an address, and an article with origin, size and class: everything you need on an empty start.
tour_ch_master_done: Supplier {tourRef} Kwekerij, customer {tourRef} Groothandel and article {tourRef} (Avocado Hass, Peru, size 18, class I) are in the system. The next chapters use them.
tour_master_vendor-new_what: We open Relations and choose New relation. First a supplier: that is where you buy.
tour_master_vendor-new_why: Suppliers and customers are both relations; one company can have both roles.
tour_master_vendor-identity_what: Search code {tourRef}-LEV, name {tourRef} Kwekerij, and we tick the Supplier role.
tour_master_vendor-identity_why: With the search code you later find the relation with a few letters and Tab, on every order.
tour_master_vendor-address_what: We add the main address: postcode, street with house number, city and country NL. We fill that in by hand here.
tour_master_vendor-address_why: The address appears on documents. A lookup by postcode and house number does not exist yet; once it does, it fills in the street and city for you.
tour_master_vendor-save_what: We save the supplier. The confirmation appears at the top.
tour_master_vendor-save_why: From now on you can buy from this supplier.
tour_master_customer-new_what: New relation again: search code {tourRef}-KLANT, name {tourRef} Groothandel, and the Customer role.
tour_master_customer-new_why: You sell to the customer; their payment and delivery terms live under the Customer role.
tour_master_customer-address_what: Here too the main address: postcode, street with house number, city and country.
tour_master_customer-address_why: You can add a delivery address separately if it differs from the main address.
tour_master_customer-save_why: From now on you can sell to this customer.
tour_master_article-new_what: We open Articles and choose New article: code {tourRef}, product Avocado, variety Hass.
tour_master_article-new_why: You type the code on every order later; the system fills in the rest of the article.
tour_master_article-origin_what: We type PE and take Peru with Tab. The country picker finds a country by name, by country code and by your own shortcut.
tour_master_article-origin_why: The country always comes from the fixed list, so 'Peru', 'PE' and 'peru' never become three different origins.
tour_master_article-size-class_what: Size 18 and class I are required; as brand we put the tour's reference, {tourRef}.
tour_master_article-size-class_why: At receiving you enter the size and class of what is actually there; that is why the article must have them. Class is one of Extra, I and II.
tour_master_article-packaging_what: Unit colli, packaging 4 kg box, weight calculated at 4 kg net per colli, and 240 colli per pallet.
tour_master_article-packaging_why: Calculated: the system derives the weight from the quantity (quantity × kg per colli), when purchasing, receiving and reserving. Choose Weighed when every pallet is actually weighed.
tour_master_article-save_why: Now you can buy and sell it.
tour_deviation_stock_what: In Availability this pallet is on Avocado Hass from {originName}, not on the ordered variant: expected, of which in inspection, until it is approved.
tour_deviation_stock_why: You sell what is really there: a customer who orders Peru does not get South Africa without anyone noticing.
tour_sales_origin_what: Each reservation shows the pallet, the lot and the purchase order this stock comes from.
tour_sales_origin_why: So with a complaint you can go straight back to the supplier and the shipment.
tour_chain_receipt_what: Receiving also shows this order's strip, with the receipt as the current step.
tour_chain_receipt_why: Whoever receives sees right away what was ordered and what happens after inspection.
tour_chain_partij_what: Under Stock › Lots is lot {partijNumber}: purchased, received, in stock and sold, with purchase order {orderNumber} in it.
tour_chain_partij_why: Everything of one shipment comes together on the lot; later also the costs and the result.
tour_ch_pinvoice_summary: Record the supplier's invoice: header, one line with an amount (12 becomes 12.00) and the totals.
tour_ch_pinvoice_done: Purchase invoice F-{tourRef} from {vendorName} is listed under Purchase invoices.
tour_pinvoice_vendor_what: We pick the supplier with Tab and type invoice number F-{tourRef}. The system calculates the due date from the payment term.
tour_pinvoice_vendor_why: Invoice date and payment term come from the supplier; that is how you know when to pay.
tour_pinvoice_line_what: One line: the article (code {productCode}), 10 pieces at 12. The amount becomes 120.00; the totals with VAT follow.
tour_pinvoice_line_why: Amounts are always shown with two decimals, in the notation of the screen language.
tour_pinvoice_save_what: We save the invoice. It now appears in the Purchase invoices list.
tour_pinvoice_save_why: Linking a purchase invoice to purchase order and receipt comes later; you already put the invoice number on the order.
settings_partij_sales_hint: Every sales order gets its own sales lot when saved, next to the order number. Its own counter; mode and restart as above.
sales_partij_hint: Suggested number; type your own number if you use one on paper.
sales_partij_hint_own: Type the number of the sales lot.
sales_partij_exists: Sales lot {number} already exists. Choose another number.
sales_partij_adjustable: Can be changed until something is reserved.
sales_partij_fixed: Fixed; correct it with a reason.
partij_list_search_sales_placeholder: Lot number, order number, customer or product
partij_sources_none: Nothing reserved yet: once you reserve, this shows which purchase lot the packages come from.
partij_sales_empty_text: A sales lot is created automatically with every sales order.
partij_sales_adjustable_hint: This sales lot belongs to one sales order. Until something is reserved or delivered, you change the number without a reason; the history is kept.
partij_sales_fixed_hint: Something has been reserved or delivered on the sales order: the number only changes with a correction and a reason.
purchase_direct_hint: For costs such as handling, transport and car hire. Goods are received through a purchase order.
purchase_invoice_exists: Invoice {number} of this supplier has already been entered.
cost_articles_hint: For invoices from third parties, such as handling, transport and QC. No stock, size, class or origin. Inactive means it can no longer be chosen; existing invoices stay as they are.
cost_article_new_placeholder: for example Electricity or Car hire
allocation_question: Which lot does this belong to?
allocation_no_rate: This invoice is in {currency} and has no ECB rate yet: you can allocate once the rate is there.
exchange_rate_line: ECB rate {date}: 1 EUR = {rate} {currency}. Costs on lots are in euro.
exchange_rate_live: Fetched from the ECB for the invoice date; again each time you open it, until costs are allocated.
exchange_rate_locked: Fixed: costs of this invoice are on lots.
exchange_rate_unavailable: The ECB rate could not be fetched right now; allocating needs a rate.
exchange_rate_unavailable_kept: The ECB rate could not be fetched again right now; the rate above still applies.
exchange_rate_none: The ECB publishes no current rate for {currency}. This invoice cannot be allocated to lots; everything stays general costs.
exchange_rate_preview_hint: The system fetches the rate from the ECB itself; you do not type it.
allocation_general: The rest, {amount}, counts as general costs.
allocation_over: Together {allocated}: more than the line amount {total} excl. VAT.
allocation_amount_invalid: Enter an amount for every lot, above 0, with at most two decimals.
allocation_conflict: Someone else has just changed this allocation.
invoice_detail_general: General costs on this invoice (not on a lot): {amount}.
partij_costs_none: No costs on this lot yet. You allocate costs from a purchase invoice:
partij_linked_costs_purchase: Separate, not in this total: costs on the sales lots with packages from this lot:
partij_linked_costs_sales: Separate, not in this total: costs on the purchase lots the packages come from:
tour_sales_partij_what: The system suggests the number of the sales lot. We leave it; on saving, the order gets this number next to its order number.
tour_sales_partij_why: On paper you work with the lot number (261140): one sale for one customer, with packages from one or more purchase lots. If you use your own numbers, type it yourself.
tour_ch_costs_summary: An invoice from a third party without a purchase order (handling € 5,000) with € 500 of it on a sales lot; the rest stays general costs.
tour_ch_costs_done: Invoice K-{tourRef}: € 500 is under Costs on sales lot {salesPartijNumber}, € 4,500 is general costs.
tour_missing_sales_lot: There is no open demo sales order with a sales lot yet.
tour_costs_invoice_what: We open Enter purchase invoice, choose supplier {vendorName} and type invoice number K-{tourRef}. No purchase order or receipt is needed.
tour_costs_invoice_why: Handling, transport, QC, electricity or car hire come on separate invoices. You enter those here directly; goods are received through a purchase order.
tour_costs_line_what: We choose the cost article Handling (group Costs) and type € 5,000 excl. VAT.
tour_costs_line_why: A cost article has no stock, size, class or origin. It sets the kind of the cost on the lot.
tour_costs_save_what: We save the invoice and open 'Allocate costs to lots'.
tour_costs_save_why: You allocate on the saved invoice, per line. Every change goes into the history.
tour_costs_choose_title: Which lot does this belong to?
tour_costs_choose_what: We choose Sales lot, search {salesPartijNumber} and put € 500 on it.
tour_costs_choose_why: Handling per customer load belongs to the sales lot; sea freight for a whole container to the purchase lot. What you do not allocate counts as general costs.
tour_costs_allocate_what: We save the allocation: € 500 on {salesPartijNumber}, € 4,500 general costs.
tour_costs_allocate_why: More than the line amount is not possible; a rest only gives a warning. Split equally, by kg or by packages works out the amounts.
tour_costs_partij_what: Sales lot {salesPartijNumber} shows under Costs: Handling, invoice K-{tourRef}, € 500.
tour_costs_partij_why: Every cost belongs to exactly one lot, so nothing counts twice. The result (sales minus purchase minus costs) comes in a later step.
packaging_lines_hint: Pallets and crates you deliver with the goods or exchange, with a quantity and a price per piece. Does nothing with stock.
packaging_load_failed: The packaging articles could not be loaded.
packaging_pallet_proposal: Proposal: {count} × {name}, from the pallets of the goods lines. You adjust it yourself afterwards.
packaging_saved_hint: Packaging is not stock: it cannot be reserved or dispatched. Quantity, price and VAT go to the sales invoice later.
packaging_error_price: 0 or more, with at most 2 decimals (for example 7.50).
packaging_line_hint: Packaging: no stock; counts as costs, general or on a lot.
packaging_articles_hint: Pallets and crates for a sales order, or charged by a supplier. No stock, size or class. The default price is a proposal on the order line; you adjust it there per order.
tour_sales_packaging_what: Add pallet puts a Pallet wegwerp (disposable pallet) line under the goods. The quantity is a proposal from the pallets of the lines; you adjust it yourself.
tour_sales_packaging_why: Packaging is on the order with quantity and price, so it reaches the invoice later. It does nothing with stock: you do not reserve or dispatch it.
ai_upload_hint: PDF, JPG, PNG or HEIC (phone photo), up to 10 MB. The AI ({model}, fallback {fallback}) makes a proposal; you check and approve it.
ai_reading: The invoice is being read by {model}… This usually takes 5 to 20 seconds.
ai_off_admin: An administrator can turn it on in Settings.
ai_status_failed: Could not check whether AI reading is on. Manual entry still works.
ai_close_failed: The proposal could not be closed; nothing has changed. Please try again.
ai_attachment_failed: The attachment could not be opened. Please try again.
ai_error_AI_OFF: AI reading is off. Enter the invoice manually.
ai_error_AI_NOT_CONFIGURED: AI reading is not set up (key or price missing). Enter the invoice manually.
ai_error_AI_RATE_LIMIT: Too many uploads in a short time. Wait a minute and try again.
ai_error_AI_MONTHLY_LIMIT: The monthly limit for AI reading has been reached; reading is paused. Manual entry still works.
ai_error_AI_UNAVAILABLE: The AI service cannot be reached, not even on a second attempt. Enter the invoice manually or try again later.
ai_error_AI_INVALID: The AI gave no usable proposal for this document. Enter the invoice manually.
ai_error_AI_UNSUPPORTED: The AI cannot read this document. Enter the invoice manually.
ai_error_AI_FAILED: AI reading failed because of an error at the provider. Enter the invoice manually.
ai_error_AI_NETWORK: No connection to the server. Try again or enter the invoice manually.
ai_error_file_tooLarge: The file is larger than 10 MB.
ai_error_file_unsupported: This file type is not supported. Use a PDF, JPG, PNG or HEIC.
ai_error_file_encrypted: The PDF is password protected. Save it without protection or enter the invoice manually.
ai_error_file_unreadable: The file is damaged or unreadable.
ai_document_unavailable: The document is no longer available.
ai_read_by_fallback: the fallback read it again because the first proposal did not add up
ai_check_yellow: The proposal does not fully add up yet: check the yellow fields.
ai_check_then_approve: Check the proposal and click Approve. What you change is recorded.
ai_order_none: No order number on the invoice: this becomes a direct invoice.
ai_order_not_found: No purchase order with order number {number}: this becomes a direct invoice.
ai_order_many: Several purchase orders with order number {number}: link the invoice later from the order.
ai_document_totals: On the invoice: excl. VAT {net} · VAT {vat} · incl. VAT {gross} {currency}
ai_problem_linesMismatch: amount does not match the lines
ai_problem_grossMismatch: total incl. VAT does not add up
ai_replace_confirm: The current draft will be replaced by the AI proposal. Continue?
ai_approved_by: AI proposal approved by {name} · read by {model}
ai_settings_hint: With AI reading, {provider} reads an uploaded purchase invoice and makes a proposal; someone checks and approves it. The document is sent to that service for this. Model: {model}, fallback: {fallback}.
ai_settings_on: AI reading is on (turned on by {name} on {date}).
ai_settings_limit_invalid: Enter an amount of 0 or more.
ai_settings_limit_reached: Monthly limit reached: {spent} of {limit}. AI reading is paused until next month or until you raise the limit; manual entry still works.
ai_settings_informed: I confirm that the customer knows documents are sent to an external AI service.
ai_detail_approved: AI proposal approved by {name} on {date} · read by {model} ({version})
tour_ch_aiinv_summary: Upload an invoice: the AI makes a proposal, you check and approve it. With the demo reader, no real AI.
tour_ch_aiinv_done: Invoice AI-{orderRef} from {vendorName} is in, approved by you; the document is attached and the invoice number is on the purchase order.
tour_aiinv_setting_what: AI reading is in Settings; it is off by default. We turn it on and confirm that the customer knows documents go to an external service.
tour_aiinv_setting_why: The AI only reads when the administrator wants it to, with a monthly limit. Who turned it on and when is recorded.
tour_aiinv_upload_what: On Enter purchase invoice we upload an invoice (PDF, photo or HEIC from a phone). The demo reader reads it right away.
tour_aiinv_upload_why: Retyping takes time and causes mistakes. The AI fills in the form; manual entry is always possible.
tour_aiinv_review_what: The document on the left, the proposal on the right in the normal form. Yellow means: the AI is unsure or it does not add up (here the date). Supplier and purchase order were found by name and order number.
tour_aiinv_review_why: The AI only proposes; you check it. What you change is recorded next to what the AI said.
tour_aiinv_approve_what: We click Approve. The invoice is saved like any invoice, with 'AI proposal approved by' you.
tour_aiinv_approve_why: Without that click the AI never saves anything. The original document is attached to the invoice, with a hash.
tour_missing_demo_reader: This chapter only works with the demo reader (DocumentAi:Reader = Demo), so a real AI call never happens.
tour_missing_ai_order: There is no demo purchase order (DEMO-TOUR-…) from the tour supplier. Play the chapter Create purchase order.
po_note_hint: Internal use only; not sent to the supplier.
po_edit_intro: You are editing order {number}. Everything stays editable until you press Make definitive or an invoice is linked; every change goes into the history.
po_edit_article_fixed: Goods have been received on this line or it has history: the article is fixed.
po_edit_min_quantity: {received} already received; it cannot be lower.
po_edit_not_removable: This line has receipts or history and stays.
po_edit_removed_in_use: Line {name} has receipts or history and cannot be removed.
po_edit_vendor_fixed: Goods have been received on this order: the supplier is fixed.
po_edit_partij_fixed: Goods have been received on this order: the lot is fixed here.
po_edit_stale: Someone else changed this order in the meantime. Reload the order and enter your change again.
po_edit_definitive_now: This order has become definitive in the meantime; you can only correct it with a reason.
po_edit_not_editable: This order cannot be edited here (customer-bound supply or cancelled).
po_finalize_confirm: After this you can no longer edit the order, only correct it with a reason. Make it definitive?
po_definitive_readonly: This order is definitive and read-only. Change a price, the supplier's order number or the note with Correction, always with a reason.
po_correct_hint: Only the price per line, the supplier's order number and the note. Quantities and articles follow from the receipt.
po_correct_reason_required: Give a reason for the correction.
po_correct_nothing: Change at least one price, the supplier's order number or the note.
po_edit_partij_kept: A lot is never removed from an order; choose another lot if needed.
po_not_found: This purchase order does not exist (any more).
tour_ch_orderedit_title: Edit an order and make it definitive
tour_ch_orderedit_summary: Edit a saved order in the same form, see the change in the history, then make it definitive and correct it with a reason.
tour_ch_orderedit_done: Order {orderNumber}: edited, made definitive and corrected with a reason; everything is in the history.
tour_orderedit_open_what: We open order {orderRef} and choose Edit.
tour_orderedit_open_why: An order stays editable until you make it definitive or an invoice is linked to it.
tour_orderedit_edit_what: The same form as when creating, filled with the order: we change the price, add a note and save.
tour_orderedit_edit_why: Once something has been received the article is fixed and the quantity cannot go below what arrived; the field says so.
tour_orderedit_history_what: Below the history is the change: who, when and per field old and new.
tour_orderedit_history_why: Nothing changes silently; the history is never overwritten.
tour_orderedit_finalize_what: We choose Make definitive and confirm the question on the page.
tour_orderedit_finalize_why: After that the order is read-only: Definitive since … by …. Receiving still works.
tour_orderedit_correct_what: On a definitive order we change the price with Correction, with a required reason.
tour_orderedit_correct_why: Only the price, the supplier's order number and the note; quantities and articles follow from the receipt.
